{{Short description|Romanian-American statistician}}
[[File:ZhouHuibin RohdeAngelika BuneaFlorentina MFO22546.jpg|thumb|''Left to right:'' Huibin Zhou, Angelika Rohde, and Florentina Bunea organized the 2018 [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|MFO]] Workshop ''Matrix Estimation Meets Statistical Network Analysis''.]]
'''Florentina Bunea''' {{r|born}} is a Romanian-American statistician, interested in [[machine learning]], the theory of [[empirical process]]es, and [[high-dimensional statistics]]. She is a professor at [[Cornell University]].

==Education and career==
Bunea earned Bachelor's and master's degrees at the [[University of Bucharest]] in 1989 and 1991. After working as an assistant professor at the [[Politehnica University of Bucharest]] from 1991 to 1995, she returned to graduate study at the [[University of Washington]].{{r|cv}} She earned her Ph.D. there in 2000; her dissertation, ''A Model Selection Approach to Partially Linear Regression'', was supervised by [[Jon A. Wellner]].{{r|mg}}

She joined the statistics faculty at [[Florida State University]] in 2000,{{r|cv|fsu}} and moved to Cornell University in 2011.{{r|cv|corn}} At Cornell, she is a faculty member in the Department of Statistics and Data Science, a member of the Center for Applied Mathematics and the Machine Learning Group in Cornell Computing and Information Science (CIS).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stat.cornell.edu/people/faculty/florentina-bunea|title=Florentina Bunea|date=2013-07-09|website=Cornell University Department of Statistics and Data Science|language=en|access-date=2019-10-06}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2017, Bunea was elected as a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].{{r|cv|fims}}
